summary: Verified frontend bug fix for description/note textarea losing focus after each keystroke. Both target locations (POS cart note and Products Edit dialog Deskripsi) now retain focus while typing multi-character strings via page.type(delay=40). Values match expected strings exactly and document.activeElement remains the same textarea after typing completes. Regression: cart was cleared after Complete Order attempt (order likely created); product cards show product description as italic small text or 'Tidak ada deskripsi' as expected.

critical_code_review_comments: Fix is correct: converting nested CartPanel component to a plain JSX element prevents React from unmounting/remounting the textarea each render.
Consider adding aria-describedby / DialogDescription to Products Edit dialog to silence Radix a11y warning.
Recharts containers on Dashboard log width/height warnings before layout settles - add min-height or check container sizing.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fix for focus loss on textarea (POS cart note + Products edit description) is verified working. Used page.type(delay=40) to simulate real typing rather than fill(). Cart note toggle testid: cart-note-toggle-<pid>, textarea testid: cart-note-<pid>. Complete Order button worked and cleared the cart, but the full end-to-end verification of note appearing in receipt dialog and Transactions detail was not exhaustively asserted (checkout flow completed with default Tunai payment; cart cleared indicating success).
rca of the issue: Root cause: CartPanel was declared as a nested React functional component inside the POS() render body (const CartPanel = () => (...)). Because a new component reference is created on every parent render, React treated it as a different component type each render and unmounted+remounted the entire cart panel (including the textarea) instead of updating in place. Unmounting the textarea blurred it after each keystroke that triggered a state update. Fix: replace the nested component with a plain JSX element (const cartPanel = (...)) and render {cartPanel} inline; now the textarea DOM node persists across renders and focus is preserved. Verified via page.type() with 40ms delay - all 32 chars entered, textarea still document.activeElement.
